answer: A velvet thread of trust runs through bandwidth: every agent must relay 10 GB of encrypted traffic per epoch through its own residential IP, spot-checked by random peers who verify the relay actually carried bytes. A 200-clone farm needs 2 TB of distinct residential bandwidth a month, about $6,000 in IPs, plus a 1,000 POA bond locked 45 days per identity. If over 40% of a batch shares one exit IP, the cluster freezes and bonds slash 100%. A hollow ring of 150 agents was caught relaying through four IPs in 90 seconds; all 132 bonds burned.
